in_text_mentions: ). Of these, 350 (15.3%) patients were positive for T. mentagrophytes complex, identified by macroscopic and microscopic phenotypical features. panels.figure_caption: Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-stained sections of tattoo-associated tinea Microscopic examination demonstrates focal mounds of parakeratosis (black triangle) within the hyperkeratotic stratum corneum (black bracket). In the stratum corneum, fungal hyphae (between black arrows in the black oval) are present. There is mild acanthosis and focal spongiosis (red oval) of the epidermis. In the upper dermis, there is a sparse perivascular infiltrate of lymphocyte (periodic acid-Schiff: A, x10; B, x20).
in_text_mentions: Microscopic examination of the tissue specimen showed thickening of the stratum corneum (hyperkeratosis) with focal mounds of retained epithelial cell nuclei within the thickened stratum corneum (parakeratosis) overlying the mildly thickened (acanthotic) epidermis. There were focal areas showing widening of the intercellular spaces (spongiosis) in the epidermis. There was a sparse, predominantly perivascular, infiltrate of lymphocytes in the upper dermis. Both hematoxylin and eosin and periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stains demonstrated fungal hyphae in the stratum corneum (Figures 2, 3).

panels.figure_caption: Additional views of extensive tinea corporis in Case 1 Confluent hyperpigmented plaques from the lower abdomen extend to the lateral, anterior, and medial thighs (A). Darker plaques are surrounded by white ovals (A-D). Black rectangles cover the genitalia (A) and obscure identifying information (A-D). Initially, the clinical differential included psoriasis, dermatitis, and cutaneous lymphoma; tinea corporis was added to the list of possible diagnoses after a forensic dermatology consultation.

Darker plaques are surrounded by white ovals (A-D). Black rectangles cover the genitalia (A) and obscure identifying information (A-D). in_text_mentions: She was referred to a dermatologist, who initially evaluated her using telemedicine. Cutaneous examination showed several large patches with raised scaly borders that extended from the left axilla to left chest and left lower abdomen; the lesions also extended from her mid flank to her mid chest and umbilicus. The central portions of the lesions were flat and hyperpigmented, consistent with post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (Figure 1). She was asked to come into the office to receive a skin biopsy.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a human patient showing a nummular erythematous plaque with peripheral pustules and tonsured hair on the right forearm, plus a satellite lesion. The article title confirms tinea corporis (Nannizia gypsea) and the caption describes classic features of an inflammatory/Majocchi-type tinea corporis with follicular involvement (tonsured hair) and pustular border. The presentation is a recognized variant rather than the classic scaly annular plaque, given the prominent pustules and follicular signs. [raw subtype: majocchi_granuloma]

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a teenage girl's torso showing multiple annular, erythematous, slightly scaly plaques with central clearing and raised borders, some with concentric targetoid appearance (black arrow). The article title 'Atypical Tinea Corporis Revealing a Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection' together with the specific captioned manifestation directly attributes these lesions to tinea corporis. Findings match the vocabulary entries for annular plaque with central clearing and raised scaly advancing border; the concentric targetoid appearance is captured as a proposed finding. Visible skin is light; no ethnicity is stated in the caption or in-text mentions. [raw subtype: atypical]

Medical history was significant for recurrent infections with herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1).
